correctness.rationale: For all k>=1 and strictly positive real masses/penalties, the scalar monotone hub KKT equation gives the unique proximal fit. After rescaling tau=1/lambda, at every upper clipping contact all incident affine slopes of v-tau*y_i are nonnegative, and at every lower contact all are nonpositive, provided m_i sum_{j!=i} a_j <= (m0+mi) a_i. This prevents exits even at simultaneous events; a separate small-lambda block argument covers initial ties. If one inequality fails, observations with one low leaf and other leaves sufficiently high create a strict positive-length fused interval and a subsequent separation. Diagonal-dominance and design-budget equivalences follow by exact algebra. Explicit four-leaf rational solution is verified by KKT. Standard-library exact rational checker passed 175512 independent sampled comparisons, supportive but not the proof.

originality.rationale: This is a sharp converse and penalty-existence classification for weighted stars, not a claim of new diagonal-dominance sufficiency. Tibshirani--Taylor 2011 Section 6 already implies the sufficient half. Hoefling 2009 provides general split-detecting path machinery and Chiquet et al. 2014 gives complete-pair data-dependent sufficient families, neither of which states the weighted-star necessary implication or exact mass budget. published-finding corpus records for star Gini/Huber sensitivity concern input perturbation norms rather than the regularization parameter fusion event. Historical overlap remains possible.
residual_risks: The sufficient half is explicitly known from the generalized-lasso row-dominance criterion; its algebraic restatement is not independently new.
An unindexed, unpublished or currently inaccessible source may already establish the star converse; the searchable corpus is not a uniqueness certificate.
No independent mathematical audit has yet checked the proof, especially simultaneous clipping transitions and universal parameter quantifiers.

value.rationale: No-split fusion paths are a central condition for whether a proximal homotopy algorithm may irreversibly merge fitted groups. The result converts a general sufficient dominance check into a complete necessary-and-sufficient criterion on a fundamental branching family, locates the first universal obstruction at four equal-mass leaves, and gives the exact hub-mass threshold for whether any fixed positive edge-weight design exists. These structural classifications distinguish fixed-star data-independent regimes and are not a tiny numerical gain or an arbitrary slice.
